status_policy: Only accepted gaps may anchor the primary idea. Candidate gaps are not evidence of a fact.

gaps.title: No auditable cross-domain xenograft-readiness framework
gaps.why_it_matters: Single-domain efficacy claims obscure deployment blockers in other domains.
gaps.falsifiable_direction: Test whether a domain-separated readiness model changes classification compared with biological-only assessment.

gaps.title: Missing bridge from graft outcome to shortage-relief capacity
gaps.why_it_matters: The number of source organs is not equal to safe, qualified, accessible graft supply.
gaps.falsifiable_direction: Model whether plausible biological success remains non-deployable when capacity, quality, surveillance, or access constraints fail.

gaps.title: Infection governance and long-term follow-up are insufficiently integrated with readiness claims
gaps.why_it_matters: A favorable early graft signal cannot justify ordinary deployment if surveillance cannot be sustained.
gaps.falsifiable_direction: Require infection-governance conditions as non-compensatory gates in readiness classification.

gaps.title: Unclear transferability between evidence settings
gaps.why_it_matters: Brain-dead human and nonhuman-primate results offer different signals and cannot be pooled as if equivalent.
gaps.falsifiable_direction: Represent evidence setting and observation horizon explicitly; abstain when transfer assumptions dominate.

rejected_or_deferred.title: Xenotransplantation already solves donor-organ shortage
rejected_or_deferred.reason: No identified evidence establishes durable, scalable, equitable deployment across the shortage landscape.

rejected_or_deferred.title: One standardized genetic modification set will suffice for all organs and indications
rejected_or_deferred.reason: Organ-specific biological and translational heterogeneity is material.
